content: CONFIRMED — `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\applications\ji-host-core\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\host\MemoryHostStore.java:72-81` declares `timeline` as `synchronized` and calls `document.snapshot().transcript()` before applying the requested limit. `SessionDocument.snapshot()` calls `entries()`, which replays and sorts the entire mutation log, constructs complete projections, and then materializes every transcript message (`E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\core\ji-session-api\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\session\tree\SessionDocument.java:65-78,1001-1003,1646-1712`). Only afterward does `timeline` select the requested window, whose REST default is 50 (`E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\applications\ji-host-web\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\host\web\LocalHostServer.java:269-285`). Because Java intrinsic synchronization covers the whole `MemoryHostStore` instance, this work blocks operations across all sessions in that store. This is realistic for Stage 4 embedded/custom deployments: the architecture explicitly supports memory and custom stores (`E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\docs\java-rewrite\02-target-architecture.md:67-76`), while Stage 4 includes the cursor timeline (`E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\docs\java-rewrite\10-roadmap-and-risks.md:142-150`). The default standalone CLI’s SQLite path is unaffected because it uses an indexed `ORDER BY … LIMIT limit+1` query.
